_comment: Confidence overrides for individual YARA rule identifiers. Any rule not listed falls back to 'default'. Use this to downgrade known-noisy rules (documented false positives, generic byte patterns, structural ZIP matchers) WITHOUT editing vendor rule files. A 'low' rule can still fire, but on its own it only reaches 'suspicious', never 'malicious'.
_how_to_tune: Run yara_debug.py against a folder of KNOWN-BENIGN apks (Telegram, Flo, F-Droid apps, etc). Every rule that matches a clean app is a false-positive source: add it here as 'low'. Remove any precautionary downgrade below that does NOT fire on your benign set, so real detections keep full weight.

_downgrade_notes.android_meterpreter: condition 'any of ($check*) or any of ($stop*)' with strings like 'eval' and 'META-INF/PK' -> matches almost every APK. Confirmed broad.
_downgrade_notes.finspy: single regex on the ZIP central-directory header with '#re > 50' -> a structural 'large archive' matcher, not FinSpy-specific. Precautionary; confirm with yara_debug.py.
_downgrade_notes.Trojan_Dendroid: condition '3 of them' over generic .php endpoint paths (/get.php?, /message.php?). Precautionary; confirm with yara_debug.py.
